_about: Clause-claim pairs train and test the verifier (data/processed/nli/pairs.jsonl, 729 pairs
= 243 clause-label matches x 3). 'premise' is the clause from the license that expresses
the label; 'hypothesis' is the claim. For each match we write three claims from templates,
so the right answer is known in advance: entailment (a true sentence for this label),
contradiction (the same sentence made opposite) and neutral (a true sentence for a
different label, which this clause does not say). Two people checked 146 pairs by hand

_about_human_check: A pair the people checking corrected (from data/processed/nli/review_labelled.csv). It was
built as neutral (a sentence for a different label), but this clause does say it, so the
right answer is entailment. 'auto_label' is the verdict from how the pair was built;
'human_label' is the checked one, which is used for training and testing.
